
=== 1. is the conntrack event stream usable at all ===
conntrack: /usr/sbin/conntrack
nf_conntrack_events: 2

=== 2a. does conntrack -E flush per event when its output is not a terminal ===
The whole page is a live tail, so an event that sits in a stdio buffer
until the next 4 KB is as good as lost. Check by hand:
    conntrack -E -e NEW | cat
and confirm rows appear as they happen rather than in bursts. If they
burst, this conntrack build is block buffering and the accept feed
needs an unbuffering wrapper.

=== 2. the load bearing assumption: a denied packet must NOT produce a NEW event ===
A conntrack entry is only confirmed once the packet has survived the
ruleset, so a dropped or rejected packet should never appear as NEW.
Check this by hand: from outside, hit a port the wan zone refuses
while watching conntrack -E -e NEW. If denied packets DO show up,
the accept feed is wrong and the design needs log based accepts.

=== 3. what fw4 logs today, and with what prefix text ===
137:		log prefix "reject lan forward: "
174:		log prefix "reject wan forward: "
178:		meta nfproto ipv4 oifname { "br-wan", "br-wan2" } ct state invalid counter log prefix "drop wan invalid ct state: " drop comment "!fw4: Prevent NAT leakage"
183:		iifname { "br-wan", "br-wan2" } counter log prefix "reject wan in: " jump handle_reject comment "!fw4: reject wan IPv4/IPv6 traffic"
187:		oifname { "br-wan", "br-wan2" } counter log prefix "reject wan out: " jump handle_reject comment "!fw4: reject wan IPv4/IPv6 traffic"
202:		log prefix "reject iot forward: "
228:		log prefix "reject vpn forward: "
261:		log prefix "reject guest forward: "
272:		iifname "br-guest" counter log prefix "reject guest in: " jump handle_reject comment "!fw4: reject guest IPv4/IPv6 traffic"
--- uci
firewall.@zone[0].log='1'
firewall.@zone[1].log='1'
firewall.iot.log='1'
firewall.@zone[3].log='1'
firewall.@zone[4].log='1'

=== 4. zones and their logging state ===
@zone[0] name=lan log=1
@zone[1] name=wan log=1
@zone[2] name=iot log=1
@zone[3] name=vpn log=1
@zone[4] name=guest log=1

=== versions ===
DISTRIB_ID='OpenWrt'
DISTRIB_RELEASE='24.10.5'
DISTRIB_REVISION='r29087-d9c5716d1d'
DISTRIB_TARGET='mediatek/filogic'
DISTRIB_ARCH='aarch64_cortex-a53'
DISTRIB_DESCRIPTION='OpenWrt 24.10.5 r29087-d9c5716d1d'
DISTRIB_TAINTS=''
Usage:

  /sbin/fw4 [-v] [-q] start|stop|flush|restart|reload

    Start, stop, flush, restart or reload the firewall respectively.


  /sbin/fw4 [-v] [-q] reload-sets

    Reload the contents of all declared sets but do not touch the
    ruleset.


  /sbin/fw4 [-q] print

    Print the rendered ruleset.


  /sbin/fw4 [-q] check

    Test the rendered ruleset using nftables' check mode without
    applying it to the running system.


  /sbin/fw4 [-q] network {net}

    Print the name of the firewall zone covering the given network.

    Exits with code 1 if the network is not found or if no zone is
    covering it.


  /sbin/fw4 [-q] device {dev}

    Print the name of the firewall zone covering the given device.

    Exits with code 1 if the device is not found or if no zone is
    covering it.


  /sbin/fw4 [-q] zone {zone} [dev]

    Print all covered devices of the given zone, optionally restricted
    to only the given device name.

    Exits with code 1 if zone is not found or if a device is specified
    and not covered by the given zone.

conntrack v1.4.8 (conntrack-tools)
